clue.text: It's extremely 'allucinogenic, indeed

indicators.note: extremely is read as at the extremes, so only the end letters of each word are taken

explanation.surface: A Cockney speaker drops the H while agreeing that something is very mind-bending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' takes the outer letters of 'allucinogenic (A, C) and indeed (I, D). The whole clue is also the definition: LSD is a famously hallucinogenic drug, and the dropped H is just Cockney flavour.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid is the street name for LSD, a drug known for causing hallucinations.

clue.text: Onset of panic as radio broadcast results in people scattering

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters are thrown into a new order
the onset of a word is where it begins, so its opening letter is taken

explanation.surface: Panic spreads after a radio broadcast, sending people fleeing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Onset of' gives P from panic; 'broadcast' rearranges P plus AS RADIO into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diaspora is the dispersal of a people from their homeland, a scattering across the world.

clue.text: Occasion for merrymaking a lot, from what we hear

indicators.note: what we hear signals that the word is said aloud and a different spelling is entered

parts.note: one's lot in life is one's fate, destiny

explanation.surface: Someone describes a big party they have been told about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a lot' looks like 'a great deal', but it means one's lot or destiny.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor festival or fair held for celebration and fundraising.

clue.text: Be critical about an expert supposedly solving everything

indicators.note: about means surrounding here, so the first piece wraps round the others

parts.note: to pan something is to criticise it harshly
taken as written
an ace is an expert, someone highly skilled

explanation.surface: A sceptic scoffs at a pundit who claims to have all the answers.
explanation.definitionFit: Something panacean acts like a cure-all, a remedy claimed to fix every problem.

clue.text: University vote in Yale should upset author

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the rearranged letters
upset means knocked over or disturbed, so the letters are put in a new order

parts.note: a voter marks an X on the ballot paper

explanation.surface: A ballot at an American college is expected to annoy a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges YALE SHOULD into ALDOUSHLEY, and 'in' puts UX into it to give ALDOUS HUXLEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Aldous Huxley was the English writer of Brave New World and other novels.

clue.text: Victory, say, by oarsman who produces vintage result?

parts.note: a victory is a win
say introduces an example, abbreviated e.g.
an oarsman is a rower

explanation.surface: A boat race win is celebrated as a fine crop of results.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a rowing victory being 'vintage'; in fact the pieces just run in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A grape farmer grows the crop whose harvest becomes a vintage of wine.

clue.text: See 5
River that's between two countries, such as India and Pakistan

definitions.meaning: a river in Hampshire, England, famed for trout fishing

definitions.text: between two countries, such as India and Pakistan
definitions.meaning: a ... match is an international cricket match played between two national sides

explanation.surface: A river forms the border between two rival nations.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a border river, but the second half is cricket: a Test is a full international match, such as India against Pakistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a Hampshire chalk stream and a full international cricket fixture.

clue.text: Land producing either cold or hot stuff, so to speak

indicators.note: so to speak signals the word is spoken, entered with a different spelling

parts.note: cold is chilly and hot stuff is chilli, and both are said the same way

explanation.surface: A country known for both cold weather and fiery food.
explanation.walkthrough: Either reading works: chilly (cold) and chilli (hot pepper) both sound like the South American country.
explanation.definitionFit: Chile is a country, a land on the Pacific coast of South America.

clue.text: Doctor I use later, without any urgency

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A patient says they will see a physician some other time.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something at leisure means taking one's time, with no hurry.

clue.text: Reckless evildoer does wrong, taking in silly padre

indicators.note: taking in means swallowing, so the first set of letters goes round the second
wrong means set awry, so the letters are rearranged
silly means muddled, so these letters too are jumbled

explanation.surface: A villain misbehaves and tricks a foolish priest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' turns DOES into DES...O, and 'silly' turns PADRE into PERAD, which is 'taken in'.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a bold, reckless outlaw ready to commit any crime.

clue.text: Story brought back about clubs providing brilliant display

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the turned word goes round the letter
brought back means returned, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a tale is a story
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games

explanation.surface: A tale about a golf club leads to a dazzling show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought back' turns TALE into ELAT, and 'about' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eclat is a striking show of success or brilliance, a dazzling effect.

clue.text: Work of 23, originating in 9 or 29, say

annotationWithheld.clue: Work of 23, originating in 9 or 29, say

clue.text: Story with moral that can make fellow clever

parts.note: an able person is clever, skilful

explanation.surface: A tale with a lesson can turn an ordinary chap into a smart one.
explanation.definitionFit: A fable is a short tale, often with animal characters, teaching a moral lesson.

clue.text: Play male part-timer in big match

indicators.note: in places the two short pieces inside the larger word

parts.note: a Test is a major international cricket match
he is the male pronoun
a temp is a temporary worker hired for a short time

explanation.surface: A man who works part-time gets to play in an important fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Play' looks like a verb about the temp playing in the match; it is the definition, a Shakespeare play. A Test is a full international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's late drama about Prospero and his island is a well-known play.

clue.text: Furtively watch over artist's kind of paint?

indicators.note: over means covering, so the phrase goes round the other piece

parts.note: to spy on someone is to watch them secretly
RA stands for Royal Academician, a distinguished artist

explanation.surface: Someone secretly keeps an eye on what a painter is using.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' wraps SPY ON round RA; RA (Royal Academician) is a crossword favourite for an artist.
explanation.definitionFit: Paint sold in aerosol cans to be sprayed rather than brushed is a type of finish.

clue.text: She's in new opera coming up

definitions.note: the definition reads as 'she is', a woman's name standing for a woman

indicators.note: coming up in a down clue means rising, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: Aida is Verdi's opera

explanation.surface: A singer is cast in a fresh opera production soon to open.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'coming up' means read upwards. 'She's' reads as 'she is', the woman standing for her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Nadia is a woman's given name, so any she could be called it.

clue.text: Novel utterance from 25, originally in 14

definitions.meaning: Aldous Huxley's dystopian novel bears this title
Miranda in The Tempest exclaims 'O ..., that has such people in't!'

explanation.surface: A remark from a character first appears in a play.
explanation.walkthrough: Huxley (5/7 down) took his title from Miranda's line in The Tempest, so both definitions name the same phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both Huxley's book title and Miranda's exclamation in Shakespeare's play.

clue.text: Dr Low, possibly, providing answer to all our ills

parts.note: DR LOW is a fresh arrangement of the letters of the globe's name, so the clue words are what the phrase describes

explanation.surface: A doctor called Low might have the cure for everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Taken as instructions, the answer describes a rearrangement of WORLD, and DR LOW is one such rearrangement; 'possibly' says it is only one of several.
explanation.definitionFit: A new world order is the grand political rearrangement proposed as a remedy for global problems.

clue.text: We must accept sultan's people are philanderers

indicators.note: accept means take in, so the first word holds the second inside it

parts.note: Oman is ruled by a sultan, so its people are Omanis

explanation.surface: A group insists on welcoming a ruler's subjects.
explanation.walkthrough: Oman is a sultanate on the Arabian Peninsula, so its people are a sultan's subjects.
explanation.definitionFit: To womanise is to chase women; philanderers are men who keep doing so.

clue.text: See 13, 17 and 18
Desiring change in location close to fighting

indicators.note: change means alter, so the letters of the word are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A wish to move closer to the action.
explanation.definitionFit: The seats next to a boxing ring are right beside the fight.

clue.text: Like either part of eternity ring

definitions.text: Like either part of eternity ring

parts.words: Like either part of eternity ring
parts.note: eternity has no finish in time, and a ring has no finish in shape, so one word describes both halves

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes a band given to symbolise lasting love.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without end is everlasting, as eternity is, or circular, as a ring is.

clue.text: Composer, having drunk vodka, runs inside

indicators.note: inside signals the letter goes into the middle of the other piece
drunk means intoxicated, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A musician drinks spirits and dashes indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' turns VODKA into DVOAK, and 'inside' places R in it.
explanation.definitionFit: Antonin Dvorak was a Czech composer, best known for the New World Symphony.

clue.text: Aspect of character first seen in Sunday school

parts.note: to school someone is to train them

explanation.surface: A trait first noticed in a church class for children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' looks like a noun, but here it is the verb to train. 'first seen in' places S at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: A strain is a streak or tendency in someone's nature, such as a strain of melancholy.

clue.text: Male golf club admitting one female

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the R and A (Royal and Ancient) is the golf club at St Andrews that governs the game
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A men-only golf club lets in a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf club' looks like an iron or driver; it is the R and A, the St Andrews club in Scotland that governs golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a woman's name, famously Prospero's daughter, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Set to become more mature after departure of Bush?

indicators.note: departure means leaving, so the letter is removed from the phrase

parts.note: to grow up is to become more mature
George W. Bush was known simply as W

explanation.surface: A question of whether politics will grow up once a president leaves office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' is the US president George W. Bush, nicknamed W.
explanation.definitionFit: A set is a collection of things belonging together, a group.

clue.text: Serving Americans, time is the essence

parts.note: GIs are US soldiers on active service

explanation.surface: For soldiers on duty, timing is the crucial point.
explanation.definitionFit: The gist of something is its core meaning, the main point.

clue.text: Feasible ideas raised for silver collectors

parts.note: a runner is an idea that could work, as in 'that plan is a non-runner' for a failed one
something raised is up

explanation.surface: Workable plans are put forward by those who collect silverware.
explanation.walkthrough: 'silver' means silver medals, which go to those finishing second.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who finish second in a contest collect the silver medals.

clue.text: School from middle of fifteenth century

indicators.note: the middle of a word is its centre letter, here the fifth of nine

parts.note: a ton is a hundred, as in a century of runs in cricket

explanation.surface: An institution founded in the mid-1400s.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is true: Eton was founded in 1440, but 'century' gives TON, a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: Eton College is a famous English public school near Windsor.

clue.text: Instruction about fitness before game for country

parts.note: PE is physical education, school lessons in fitness
RU is rugby union

explanation.surface: A coach gives fitness instructions before a match abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: Peru is a country in South America.

clue.text: Furs close family put in vessel

parts.note: to seal something is to close it

indicators.note: put in means placed inside, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: SS is a steamship, a vessel
kin is family

explanation.surface: Relatives load expensive furs onto a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like an adjective for the family; it is the verb to seal.
explanation.definitionFit: Sealskins are the pelts of seals, used as furs.
